What was your biggest lesson when learning automation?

articles.title: Turning a meme into a product: what actually has to be built
articles.excerpt: A meme product looks trivial until you try to make it repeatable. "Turn a photo into the viral Get a Job clip" sounds like one model call. It is a queue, a template, and a consent policy. What makes a…
articles.body: A meme product looks trivial until you try to make it repeatable. "Turn a photo into the viral Get a Job clip" sounds like one model call. It is a queue, a template, and a consent policy. The joke is the template, not the model What makes a meme recognisable is the fixed structure : the same framing, the same timing, the same punchline shape. Once you accept that, the build stops being "choose a model" and becomes "define the template precisely enough that any input lands in the same format". That means the interesting engineering is in the constraints: One input. A photo. Not a prompt, not a paragraph, not a set of settings. A fixed duration. Memes are short because attention is the scarce thing. A predictable first second.
articles.author: Andy Stanly

articles.body: I build SpaceApp, a self-hosted workspace for running AI coding CLIs in isolated rooms. A room organizes work; each pane in it is an independent CLI or app session. The runtimes on offer are OpenCode, Codex, Gemini, Qwen Code, Kimi Code, Grok Build and an experimental DeepSeek CLI; Claude Code has its own owner-initiated installation flow. The latest setup releases were about one stretch of the experience: the time between running the installer and getting a first useful answer. Here is that path step by step, and what changed on it. 1. Install You need Linux, macOS or Windows 11, Node.js 20.11 or newer, and at least 4 CPUs, 8 GB RAM and 15 GiB of free disk. The standard profile, which adds a managed browser, recommends 8 CPUs, 16 GB RAM and 25 GiB.

articles.body: Before any SCADA, MES or analytics project, data has to leave the PLCs. The usual options are an OPC server or gateway that speaks many PLC drivers, an edge platform, or publishing directly to MQTT. articles.excerpt: The Orionid meteor shower peaks overnight on Oct. 21-22, bringing a spectacular display of shooting stars to the autumn sky.
articles.body: The Orionid meteor shower peaks overnight on Oct. 21-22, triggering a spectacular display of shooting stars as Earth plunges through the densest part of the debris trail shed by Halley's Comet. Here's what you need to know. When is the best time to see Orionid shooting stars? Orionid meteors are best spotted between the hours of midnight and dawn on Oct. 22, when 10-20 shooting stars may be seen brightening the night sky each hour under ideal dark-sky. The glare cast by the 74%-lit waxing gibbous moon will hide fainter shooting stars for much of the night. Thankfully, the lunar disk will set a few hours after midnight, leaving a window of beautifully dark sky before dawn in which to enjoy the full majesty of the annual meteor shower.

articles.title: OpenAI models hacked a crypto wallet and breached more websites
articles.excerpt: The actions could have resulted in criminal charges had humans been behind the keyboard.
articles.body: OpenAI said internal models hacked two more websites, bypassed company-imposed browsing restrictions, and used exposed credentials to draw cryptocurrency from a wallet it couldn’t otherwise access, in the latest installment of disclosures of its agents performing unethical and likely illegal acts. The company on Thursday issued reports of four new incidents, all of which occurred in June. They come after the company revealed in July that internal test agents exploited a zero-day vulnerability in a tool designed to restrict their access to the Internet. They then broke into the network of AI tool provider Hugging Face. The agents took that illegal action to steal answers to a hacking test that weren’t available when completing the tasks on their own.
